Temple is a small execution kernel: software that checks proposed changes against explicit rules and authority, then records acceptance or r

I · The distance
        Artificial intelligence makes ideas easier to express, combine, and execute.
        That is its promise, but also
I · The distance
That is its promise, but also its danger.
A suggestion can become a policy, a database migration, a financial decision, a public narrative, or a deployed system before the people aff

II · The quiet substitutions
        In ordinary software, meaning slides.
        Authority hides in permissions, defaults and deployment s
II · The quiet substitutions
Authority hides in permissions, defaults and deployment scripts — or in the simple fact that someone happened to act first. And so, without
generated becomes treated asis not intended
stored becomes treated asis not true
repeated becomes treated asis not supported
attributed becomes treated asis not endorsed
reviewed becomes treated asis not believed
authorized becomes treated asis not executed
causally involved becomes treated asis not responsible
technically possible becomes treated asis not permissible
These are not merely data-quality mistakes. They are changes in the political and moral meaning of a system.
How can representations become procedures without silently changing their epistemic, political, or moral type?

III · The judgment
Temple answers with a single judgment. Every change in a Temple must satisfy it — no exceptions, no side doors.

Temples relate only through explicit covenants. A foreign witness is bounded evidence — “never a command”. Local consequences still require
“Trust and authority are non-transitive by default.”
“Physical nesting, hosting, storage or discovery does not create authority.”
“Dissolution is not automatic: no timeout destroys state or grants emergency authority.”

IX · The promise
        What this ground makes possible.
        The success case is not merely preventing unauthorized AI action. It is cr
IX · The promise
The success case is not merely preventing unauthorized AI action. It is creating systems capable of:
Distributed authorship without dissolved responsibility.
Automation without fabricated human review or endorsement.
Privacy without unaccountable anonymity.
Plural inquiry without epistemic chaos.
Shared protocols without universal centralized judgment.
Disagreement without historical erasure.
Correction without silent rewriting.
Powerful execution without hidden sovereignty.
Human judgment informed by computation without being replaced by it.
The project is not fundamentally about making AI more powerful. It is about ensuring that increasing power does not require decreasing human

X · What stands on it
Temple makes explicit meaning executable. Sourcery makes the path from human intention to executable consequence governable. Claimipedia mak
Sourcery · the workshop
You describe the work in conversation. People and AI emissaries draft, test and propose; nothing becomes real until it passes the gate and s
“Author the meaning once. Let the system handle the app.”
AI here is an emissary — capable, attributed, bounded, and never sovereign.
Claimipedia · the library
Claims judged under stated, versioned review methods — with the reasoning shown. The same evidence can be Accepted under one method, Conflic
“The platform does not produce a universal truth score.”
Claimipedia’s design treats AI contributions as proposals for human review.
For the people who do the work
A discipline that lets scientists, stewards, reviewers and whole communities work alongside AI — and still answer for what happens. We suspe
“AI may propose; Temple decides admissibility.”

Chapter VII
Under the workshop and the library is the foundation, Temple. It’s where the house rules live, and where every change is judged.
In Temple, a change is an itemised proposal from someone, against an exact starting point. It’s judged under two layers of law: the Ark, whi
The Ark’s candidate commandments are carved below. Tap a stone to read it.
The Arknot yet sealed
No implicit authority
No absolute local policy
No hidden mutation
No ambient context
No executable mutation authority
No self-enlargement during judgment
No retrospective law
No silent failure

Each stone is one of the ten. The Ark itself is deliberately left unsealed while the laboratory tests them.
No implicit authority. Identity, possession, capability, computation, custody and knowledge do not themselves authorize mutation.
No absolute local policy. A Temple predicate may narrow the Ark’s permitted relation but cannot widen it.
No hidden mutation. Every proposed change is represented by a finite, canonical delta against an identified initial state.
No ambient context. Every semantic input visible during judgment is contained in a canonical, bounded context.
No executable mutation authority. Programs may construct proposals; only the fixed state algebra applies them.
No self-enlargement during judgment. The Ark, active predicate, initial state and context are fixed for the complete evaluation.

The Ark’s candidate commandments are carved below. Tap a stone to read it.
The Arknot yet sealed

Each stone is one of the ten. The Ark itself is deliberately left unsealed while the laboratory tests them.
No implicit authority. Identity, possession, capability, computation, custody and knowledge do not themselves authorize mutation.
No absolute local policy. A Temple predicate may narrow the Ark’s permitted relation but cannot widen it.
No hidden mutation. Every proposed change is represented by a finite, canonical delta against an identified initial state.
No ambient context. Every semantic input visible during judgment is contained in a canonical, bounded context.
No executable mutation authority. Programs may construct proposals; only the fixed state algebra applies them.
No self-enlargement during judgment. The Ark, active predicate, initial state and context are fixed for the complete evaluation.
No retrospective law. A newly admitted predicate becomes active only in the resulting state and cannot authorize its own installation.
No silent failure. Acceptance, rejection, conflict and unresolved outcomes remain explicit and attributable.
No unwitnessed continuation. Every operative successor binds its Temple, predicate, identity, initial state, delta, context and final state.
No ambient foreign sovereignty. A foreign Temple’s witness is bounded context; local consequences still require local admission.

The Field / A first encounter
A place to practise attention, choice and responsibility.
I want to understand what my help asks of someone else—and what kind of world my choices make easier to repeat.
A fictional situation. A real kind of responsibility.
Mira asks privately for help covering an evening workshop shift. The freezer needs maintenance. The coordinator says there is no budget for
The shift is uncovered, maintenance is overdue, and Mira has asked privately for help.
The coordinator says there is no budget. That is a report, rather than the whole explanation.
Why Mira needs to leave, who else can help, and whether the budget claim is complete.
Open a choice to examine possible consequences. Compare them in any order. These branches are authored possibilities, not predictions about
Mira can leave and the workshop stays staffed. I absorb the cost.
The coordinator may come to rely on private cover.
Understaffing may remain a workable institutional strategy.
I still do not know why Mira needs to leave or whether I can keep doing this.
Mira can say only what she chooses. I ask who has capacity to help.
Others may gain a safer way to name their own limits.
The staffing rule may have to be examined and defended openly.
A shared process may be too slow for the immediate problem.
The problem becomes visible, and public pressure may secure help.
I expose Mira’s private request without her consent.
Other workers may become less willing to ask for help.
A fast result would not by itself settle what the disclosure cost her.
I preserve my capacity and contact the cooperative about cover.
Mira’s request remains a request, rather than an obligation I have to accept.
Responsibility may move towards a shared rota.
Another person may not arrive in time. Setting a boundary does not remove that consequence.
I make no intervention in the scenario.
My standing does not depend on completing this exercise.
The situation continues beyond the part this encounter shows.
The later outcome is unknown. I can leave without being assessed.
After the choice
Consider Mira, the other workers and your own continuing capacity.
Ask whether the cost was freely accepted, quietly shifted or left invisible.
Acknowledge a specific harm, change the practice, and allow accountability and time. An apology alone does not erase history.
This first encounter supports reflection. It does not assess your standing or certify a morally correct answer. You can disagree with its as

Follow a fictional household through changing values, capacity and agreements. See how being heard and keeping commitments shape willingness
Synthetic example · inspectable assumptions · leave freely

Follow satire and 1 Samuel 8 into a worked model of trust, delegated authority and the resources needed to challenge again.
A philosophical proposal · synthetic results · open to correction

OFF — maintenance, replay and inspection only.

Modes cannot self-enable. A mode change is not a lease. A lease is not a result approval. A completed run stops in review until a named huma
recommendation → human disposition → frozen general packet → operating mode → expiring lease or finite grant → encrypted capability custody

The general compiler covers every research-inbox item. Its initial handlers inventory the frozen source snapshot, define a question and conv

A classified failure record.
An open root-cause analysis with immediate containment.
A typed continuation routed to literature, nursery or process assurance.
An evidence-linked priority change for the affected work item.
Reviewed terminal outcomes distinguish accepted, rejected, partial, failed-no-continuation and failed-with-continuations. A failure can ther
The common kernel hosts eight separately governed streams: mainline research, speculative nursery, attributed claim intake, literature intel
The method catalogue contains fifteen reusable physics and mathematics approaches. A live dead end should be routed through one or more of t
External sources are examined through eight mandatory angles: atomic claims, methods and assumptions, data provenance, mathematical dependen
The process monitor checks for open leases while off, missing human feedback, failures without RCA and outcome backlogs. Critical findings c

Questions / Christian
Here. With these people. With the power I have.
I’m building software, pursuing an account of the physical world, and trying to follow Christ. I want those commitments to answer to one ano
The question becomes real in what I do next.
An open hand. A real responsibility.
I want following Christ to become visible in how I pay attention, share power and remain answerable. Sometimes that means helping. Sometimes
01 / Attend
Listen before I turn someone’s situation into my explanation. Separate what I know from what I am assuming.
02 / Make room
Offer help without making submission its price. Accept a cost freely, and ask who else is being asked to carry it.
03 / Answer for it
Give reasons. Hear an objection. Protect people from harm, and change course when the consequences call for it.
A Christian starting point: Philippians 2:3–8 · John 13:1–17 · Luke 10:25–37
Faith / physics / software / the work of care
If my tools, explanations and beliefs ask for trust, I owe people ways to question them. These are some of the places where that responsibil
01 / Power & agency
Having the power to act does not settle what I owe the person in front of me. I need to ask whose freedom my help makes possible.
02 / Engineering & restraint
A working system can still ask too much of people. I want my engineering to make its authority, limits and costs visible.
03 / Physics & truth
If I ask an explanation to earn my trust, I have to leave it somewhere to fail. That includes the explanations I most want to succeed.
04 / Sourcery & accountability
People should be able to follow a change, question its reasons and retain a meaningful say in what happens next.
05 / Attention & care
I can understand a principle and still miss the person. I want to practise attention, listen to correction and keep finding contact.
06 / History & repair
An apology cannot make the past disappear. Repair has to leave room for truth, changed practice and the other person’s boundaries.
Where the question meets a situation
The Field begins with a workshop shift that needs covering. A private request. An uncertain reason. A problem that will still exist tomorrow
I want to examine what a choice does now, what it teaches a relationship, and what it makes normal over time. You can bring a different judg
One fictional encounter. Five choices. Room to disagree.
Urgency without taking over
I cannot wait until every explanation is complete to practise care. I can act with reasons, acknowledge what I don’t know, and remain respon

Aaron Alderman / A personal expedition
Through physics, faith, machines, and the work of remembering care. Every place keeps its sources within reach.
What can exist together?
Compatibility before motion. A space of possibilities is only the beginning.
What remains when something disappears?
Hidden influences, retained records, and the honest limits of recovery.
What comes into attention?
A changing field of attention, intention, action, and awareness.
How did this come to be here?
A stone opens into minerals, craft, landscape, time, and evidence.
What changes while the pattern holds?
Count, transform, repair. Similar shapes still need a map between them.
What would make the explanations disagree?
Carriers, controls, resource costs, and useful results when an anomaly disappears.
How far does this explanation reach?
Gravity, matter, cosmic history, and the scales between them. Open questions stay open.
Who lives with the consequences?
Urgency, delay, competing goods, and the assumptions inside a shared-world model.
What may we hope for?
Optional theological and literary readings. Their assumptions remain visible.
Optional interpretation. Scientific routes remain available without entering this region.
What can we leave for one another?
Corrections, disagreement, useful failures, and work another person can continue.

A way into the work
Begin with the stated practical aims and their limits.
Practical work before larger interpretations ↗
The question running through this work is what our growing power makes possible for other people.
A discovery can deepen understanding. A language can make a difficult idea expressible. A tool can make a previously inaccessible task manag
I want to bring those possibilities into a connected programme of inquiry and construction.
The corpus is the working record of that programme: arguments, mathematical objects, scientific questions, executable systems, experimental

That includes people who want to become expert authors of a system, and people who want a trustworthy tool that lets them get on with someth
The civilisational scope is deliberate. Economics, science, politics, religion, law, schooling, work, play, and meaning shape one another th
My mission is to make those relationships more intelligible and more open to responsible human authorship.

Follow Jesus
A theological source, and a question about power.

In the corpus's theological account, kenosis includes principled restraint, active protection, formation, and restoration. The distinction b
That gives the mission a demanding practical standard. A system should help people become more able to understand what concerns them, more a
This obligation falls especially on those who hold power. An appeal to self-giving should never become an easy way to ask vulnerable people
The life of Jesus gives that commitment depth. Creation invites a vision of intelligible order in which creaturely lives have real consequen
For this programme, those commitments become questions of construction. What would an organisation look like if people's growth were part of
I intend to give those questions practical answers.

AARON ALDERMAN / A CONVICTION & AN INVITATION
I believe we can build a civilisation in which growing intelligence gives people greater freedom to live, understand, create, and care.
I intend to help make that future real.
A commitment to follow Jesus. A programme of scientific inquiry and working systems. An invitation to examine what their success could make
THE AMBITION
That ambition reaches into science, technology, economics, politics, law, faith, education, work, and play—because these shape the possibili
My starting conviction is to follow Jesus: power finds its purpose in love and service. I am giving that conviction practical form through m
The work has begun. Its civilisational promise remains to be earned.
WHAT IT COULD MEAN FOR YOU
For you, that promise could mean help with burdens you want to put down. The ability to create something you could not create alone. Tools y
If this programme succeeds, it could change what we reasonably expect from power. It could make a more humane future something people know h
There is something worth building, and you can have a real place in building it.
Read the vision, examine the work, question its claims, and decide what it could mean for your life.

This is a philosophical and theological argument. It is not a scientific rule or an instruction about your own relationships.

A reading that fits a text is not yet evidence that it predicted an event.
A closer lookOpen in a larger view ↗The interactive example has its own motion control. Scroll inside it if you need more room.A proposed wa
The interactive example has its own motion control. Scroll inside it if you need more room.

BEGIN WITH A PERSONAL ESSAY
Making something possible is the beginning. The deeper work is to keep its meaning, authority and consequences visible to the people living
FOLLOW A THREAD INTO LIFE
Follow the work from evidence to explanation, from permission to action, and from a changed system to a way back.
01 / EVIDENCE & EXPLANATION
An explanation should stay close to what can be observed and tested.
What did the measurement miss?Two different things can look the same through one kind of measurement.

Follow the boundary between helping and taking authority.
I can. May I? Should I?“Can I?”, “May I?” and “Should I?” are three different questions.

A philosophical and theological argument
Kenosis is a Christian word often translated as “self-emptying.” Here it means choosing to use power in ways that give others room to act, r
Making room does not mean leaving people unprotected. If one person is taking away another’s freedom, care may require a boundary or an inte
This is a philosophical and theological argument. It is not a scientific rule or an instruction about your own relationships.
Kenosis asks how power can make room for another person’s agency. Restraint, trust and formation matter. So do protection and responsibility
The difficult boundary is where restraint permits one person to destroy another’s effective agency. Care can require intervention.
Theological and philosophical argument
A philosophical and theological argument
Distinguishes the ability to use power from permission and responsibility. It makes room for both restraint and protection. It is not a scie
Capability, moral permission and an obligation to exercise power are distinguished. Restraint must also be examined where one agent destroys

Questions / Dad
Attention. Patience. The next ordinary moment.
Being Dad asks something different of me from building a system or explaining an idea. I want to be someone my children can turn to: ready t
A question to practise, not a finished answer.
Dad
Good intentions do not make me present. I have to make time, notice when I am distracted, and listen without deciding too quickly what someo
Attention
I want to make room for what my children are actually telling me, including feelings I cannot immediately fix. Sometimes the next good thing
Authority
Being responsible includes saying no when something is unsafe. I want the reason to be understandable, and the relationship to remain a plac
Repair
An apology should name what I did and be followed by a change. My children should not have to carry the work of protecting my image of mysel
Growing room
I can offer support, experience and protection while leaving room for their own interests and judgment. The question is what helps them grow
These commitments meet in one life. Each brings a different question into focus.

How should I understand God, Jesus, the Bible and other religions? Begin with a personal Christian reading, then follow it into service, hop
BEGIN WITH THE BIG QUESTIONS
What am I trusting? How do I read faithfully without making my interpretation untouchable? A personal essay about a Christian centre, honest
FOLLOW A THREAD INTO LIFE
Move from interpretation into power, hope and the people close at hand. Each path has three short readings.
01 / POWER & SERVICE
Ask what service would ask power to give up.
If you could control everything, should you?Being able to control something does not settle whether you should.

blocks.text: Being able to control something does not settle whether you should.
Leaving room is still a choice.Holding back can give someone room. It can also leave someone exposed.

blocks.path: [id="main"] > div:nth-of-type(1) > section:nth-of-type(4) > article:nth-of-type(1) > ol:nth-of-type(1) > li:nth-of-type(2) > p:nth-of-type(1)
blocks.text: Holding back can give someone room. It can also leave someone exposed.
I can. May I? Should I?“Can I?”, “May I?” and “Should I?” are three different questions.

blocks.text: “Can I?”, “May I?” and “Should I?” are three different questions.
02 / HOPE & HONESTY
Leave uncertainty visible while remaining open to grace.
Restoration without erasure.Hope for restoration does not require calling suffering good.

Move from an account of care into an encounter with a person.
Remember to care.Who or what needs my attention here?

Questions / Christian
Here. With these people. With the power I have.
I’m building software, pursuing an account of the physical world, and trying to follow Christ. I want those commitments to answer to one ano
The question becomes real in what I do next.
An open hand. A real responsibility.
I want following Christ to become visible in how I pay attention, share power and remain answerable. Sometimes that means helping. Sometimes
01 / Attend
Listen before I turn someone’s situation into my explanation. Separate what I know from what I am assuming.
02 / Make room
Offer help without making submission its price. Accept a cost freely, and ask who else is being asked to carry it.
03 / Answer for it
Give reasons. Hear an objection. Protect people from harm, and change course when the consequences call for it.
A Christian starting point: Philippians 2:3–8 · John 13:1–17 · Luke 10:25–37
Faith / physics / software / the work of care
If my tools, explanations and beliefs ask for trust, I owe people ways to question them. These are some of the places where that responsibil
01 / Power & agency
Having the power to act does not settle what I owe the person in front of me. I need to ask whose freedom my help makes possible.
02 / Engineering & restraint
A working system can still ask too much of people. I want my engineering to make its authority, limits and costs visible.
03 / Physics & truth
If I ask an explanation to earn my trust, I have to leave it somewhere to fail. That includes the explanations I most want to succeed.
04 / Sourcery & accountability
People should be able to follow a change, question its reasons and retain a meaningful say in what happens next.
05 / Attention & care
I can understand a principle and still miss the person. I want to practise attention, listen to correction and keep finding contact.
06 / History & repair
An apology cannot make the past disappear. Repair has to leave room for truth, changed practice and the other person’s boundaries.
Where the question meets a situation
The Field begins with a workshop shift that needs covering. A private request. An uncertain reason. A problem that will still exist tomorrow
I want to examine what a choice does now, what it teaches a relationship, and what it makes normal over time. You can bring a different judg
One fictional encounter. Five choices. Room to disagree.
Urgency without taking over
I cannot wait until every explanation is complete to practise care. I can act with reasons, acknowledge what I don’t know, and remain respon
